Nexeon raises £100 million to expand its UK silicon anode operations
Posted September 9, 2026 by Chris Ruoff & filed under Newswire , The Tech . 
Oxfordshire-based silicon anode developer Nexeon has closed a £100-million ($133-million) investment round, completed by a £52.6-million ($70-million) commitment from the UK’s National Wealth Fund . The Korea Development Bank and Honda Xcelerator Ventures, Honda’s open innovation investment program, also came in as new investors. The round follows the $170 million Nexeon raised in 2022 in a round that included Ingevity.
The National Wealth Fund’s financing will go toward a UK-based pilot manufacturing facility, R&D work and an expansion of Nexeon’s advanced manufacturing technology unit. A pilot line is where a materials supplier proves out a process at intermediate scale and makes the qualification samples cell manufacturers test before anyone commits to full production volumes.
Silicon holds far more lithium per gram than the graphite it replaces in a conventional lithium-ion anode, but it expands as it takes up that lithium, and containing the expansion over hundreds of cycles is the central engineering problem for silicon anode materials . Nexeon says its materials raise cell energy density, cut charging times and extend EV driving range.
Nexeon already makes silicon-carbon materials at a volume production plant in Gunsan, South Korea. The company has said it picked the site for pipeline supply of monosilane gas, a key precursor for the material, and for its proximity to Asian cell producers. The plant is designed so that additional reactors can be installed to scale output, according to the company.
“This investment is a strong endorsement of Nexeon’s technology and our role in enabling the next generation of lithium-ion batteries. The National Wealth Fund’s support reflects the strategic importance of our work, not only in advancing battery performance but also in strengthening the UK’s position in the global battery supply chain,” said Scott Brown, CEO of Nexeon.

content_text:
Solvay confirms OneIM talks over strategic European rare-earths business
by EUToday Correspondents 
September 9, 2026 
written by EUToday Correspondents 
September 9, 2026 
Solvay confirms OneIM talks over strategic European rare-earths business
2K The Belgian chemicals group said in regulated information on 8 September that talks were continuing and that it would provide further information when appropriate. The announcement followed a Reuters report that discussions had been under way since March. OneIM did not immediately comment.
The asset at the centre of the talks is Solvay’s separation operation at La Rochelle in France. The site processes rare-earth materials used in magnets and other advanced manufacturing. Solvay describes the business as part of its broader Special Chem portfolio, which also includes fluorine products; figures for the combined portfolio should not be treated as rare-earth revenue alone.
The potential partnership comes as European governments seek alternatives to Chinese processing. Separation capacity is more difficult to build than a mine because it requires specialised chemistry, waste controls, qualified staff and long-term feedstock contracts. A change in ownership or financing could therefore affect Europe’s industrial plans even if Solvay continues to operate the plant.
Financing a supply chain
Solvay has signed a letter of intent with Brazil’s Viridis Mining and Minerals to source rare-earth feedstock for La Rochelle from the Colossus project. The arrangement is targeted for 2028 and remains subject to a definitive agreement and project development. It covers neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium, terbium and other materials that can feed magnet production.
Viridis said OneIM would invest up to $75 million and become a cornerstone investor in its Brazilian project. That is financing for the upstream development, not proof that European separation capacity has already expanded. Solvay has also discussed a €15–20 million La Rochelle expansion, with heavy rare-earth separation targeted for autumn 2026.
The possible OneIM partnership could provide capital or a different ownership structure for those plans. Solvay has not disclosed a valuation, timetable or the form of any investment. Its statement makes clear that talks may end without an agreement.
EU Today has previously covered Brussels’ plans to build a critical-minerals stockpile. The Solvay discussions show the industrial side of that policy: stockpiles can provide insurance, but processing plants require steady feedstock, financing and customers over many years.
The next formal development will be a company announcement if the parties reach binding terms. Until then, La Rochelle’s capacity, the Viridis timetable and the 2028 supply target remain separate pieces of a proposed chain. Solvay’s notice gives no valuation or closing date, so the talks cannot be treated as a completed sale.

Summary
Commitment aims to support the growth of winter canola in the Southern Great Plains of the U.S., as a feedstock for renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel 
Monheim, Germany/St. Louis, USA, September 9, 2026 – Bayer and Neste, the world’s leading producer of renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel, have finalized a commercial agreement to jointly scale Bayer’s newgold ® winter canola. 
The collaboration will enable Bayer to significantly expand acres of winter canola in the Southern Great Plains of the US, strengthening the oilseed supply potential of lower-carbon-intensity feedstocks to meet the growing global demand for biofuels such as renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel, which is estimated to increase almost threefold reaching approximately 40 billion gallons by 2040. 1,2 The high protein meal from the winter canola grain will be sold into the feed market, offering additional feed sources for dairy and beef cattle, poultry and swine markets. 
“In times of geopolitical tensions, the need for more energy security and resilience while decarbonizing the transportation sector leads to growing demand for renewable fuel. This agreement further underscores Bayer’s commitment to help scale biofuels production,” said Frank Terhorst, Head of Strategy and Sustainability for Bayer’s Crop Science division. “We see the Southern Great Plains as an untapped opportunity for winter canola. The launch of newgold ® winter canola will provide farmers with a profitable rotational crop with wheat and improve land utilization, while offering the opportunity to participate in a growing biofuels market.” 
Bayer and Neste are establishing a newgold ® network with additional value chain partners, to support the expansion of winter canola and ensure an additional market for farmers. 
“Maximizing the contribution of novel types of raw materials to support growth in renewables requires open supply chain collaboration. By building robust value chains, we can turn agricultural innovations into scalable realities for growers and energy markets. Through the Bayer newgold ® winter canola collaboration, we are establishing a value chain in one of Neste’s key markets and developing opportunities to increase farm yields and grower income. This renewable raw material can be scaled rapidly in the coming years, which can help meet increasing biofuels demand,” says Artturi Mikkola, Senior Vice President, Renewable Products Feedstock Sourcing and Trading at Neste. 
Bayer aims to launch newgold ® winter canola hybrids in the fall of 2027. These hybrids offer farmers several benefits, including winter-hardiness, TruFlex ® , Bayer’s second-generation Roundup Ready trait technology, and pod shatter resistance technology. Together, these advancements can deliver strong potential for yield performance and higher oil content. TruFlex winter canola, sold under the newgold ® seed brand, will be designed with the goal of acting as a new profit opportunity for the Southern Great Plains, giving growers the flexibility to decide how and where it fits best in their operation. 
Biofuels can play a key role in helping the transportation sector in its energy transition since electrification may not be feasible in all transportation systems like aviation, rail, heavy duty equipment or marine. Biofuels can be produced from renewable organic materials like corn, soy, canola and other intermediate oilseed crops, such as winter canola. Bayer recently presented its biofuels platform at its investor day in Huxley, IA, where it highlighted its emergent, but leading portfolio of intermediate biofuel crops, including camelina, winter canola and CoverCress™.

Infineon and SolarEdge extend collaboration
Wednesday 9th September 2026
Companies extend collaboration into solid-state circuit breaker (SSCB) technology 
Infineon and SolarEdge Technologies have extended of their collaboration to advance solid-state circuit breaker (SSCB) technology for high-voltage DC distribution in AI and hyperscale data centres. 
The collaboration addresses a key challenge in the adoption of 800 VDC architecture: Safe operation of increasingly power-dense infrastructure requires a very fast fault-isolation to achieve selectivity while maintaining high efficiency.
The compannies says that the aims is to address a critical gap in the distribution layer between the solid-state transformer (SST) and the compute rack, in order to develop a grid-to-rack solution. SolarEdge is leading the design of the SSCB solution, with Infineon providing its SiC JFET technology at the core of the protection devices.
DC protection presents different engineering challenges to AC designs. Without a natural current zero, mechanical interruption faces challenges with arcing. It is comparatively slow, and as such requires a different approach to circuit protection than conventional AC systems. 
Solid-state circuit breakers are designed to interrupt faults within a few microseconds, with no mechanical contacts to separate, while Infineon's CoolSiC JFET devices are claimed to deliver efficient operation and superior robustness. Together, these capabilities help protect high-value compute equipment and enable more compact, higher-density DC distribution designs.
The collaboration builds on SolarEdge's SST platform ( pictured above ) with Infineon SiC components, first announced in November 2025. The SST is designed to enable direct medium-voltage (13.8-34.5 kV) to 800-1500 VDC conversion at over 99 percent efficiency, collapsing multiple conversion stages into a single solution while reducing physical footprint.

The world's two biggest chipmakers have seen the (ultraviolet) light. 
ASML announced Tuesday that Samsung and TSMC agreed to adopt its high-numerical aperture (NA) extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines to manufacture semiconductors by 2028 and 2030, respectively. If that sounds like too much technical mumbo jumbo, basically it means the already flush company's photolithography machines could soon print money. 
Sign up for The Daily Upside at no cost for premium analysis on all your favorite stocks. 
READ ALSO: AI Risks, Trade War Loom Over Trump-Xi Summit and IBM Takes a Billion-Dollar Step Toward Becoming Quantum's Foundry King 
UV Monopoly Protection 
The list of companies that can make extreme ultraviolet lithography machines, which are essential to manufacturing the most advanced semiconductors for AI, smartphones and high-end computing, is as follows: ASML. This 100% commercial monopoly has helped lift shares in the Dutch firm 126% in the past year. The more AI demand intensifies, the more demand for AI infrastructure intensifies and the greater the need for ASML's machines to print the chips needed at new advanced data centers. With Wall Street forecasting trillions of dollars in AI capital expenditures for years, that cycle could run for a while. 
ASML, whose machines print microscopic circuit patterns on silicon wafers, debuted its Low NA EUV, now widely used, in 2013. What TSMC and Samsung agreed to adopt on Tuesday is more advanced High NA EUV lithography. It can print smaller features with more precision than Low NA, which means chipmakers can fit more transistors on each semiconductor, increasing their processing power. 
Barclays analysts called the announcement a "positive" for High NA EUV machines, viewed as crucial to ASML's revenue growth. ASML rose 2.91% in New York on Tuesday, and Wall Street sees room for more gains: 
The average target price of $2,414, according to Zacks Investment Research, implies the stock has a 40% upside. 
ASML, Intel, Samsung and TSMC separately agreed Tuesday to double the size of photomasks, the template stencils used to print silicon wafers with UV light, from 6 inches to 12, another step toward faster production. 
Poor Imitation: ASML's stock sank in late July following reports that a state-backed Chinese rival had begun mass-producing ultraviolet lithography tools. At the time, JPMorgan dismissed the selloff as "disproportionate," noting China has been making lower-end equipment for years "without any impact on ASML's market share." Last week, UBS analysts joined in, writing that China is years behind and unlikely to rival ASML's technology any time soon.

AI infrastructure stocks rally on deal announcements from Qualcomm, Corning
Published Tue, Sep 8 2026 6:02 PM EDT 
Isabel O'Brien @in/xisabelobrienx @xisabelobrienx 
WATCH LIVE 
Key Points
Corning and Qualcomm popped on Tuesday, and lifted other companies tied to the AI infrastructure trade, including Intel and Advanced Micro Devices.
Qualcomm announced a partnership with Amazon that included issuing $4 billion in stock warrants to the cloud provider. 
Corning disclosed a multibillion-dollar deal with Verizon to build fiber-optic cables for AI connectivity.

Corning CEO Wendell Weeks talks to CNBC's Katie Tarasov at Corning's cable factory in Hickory, North Carolina, on Jan. 9, 2026.
Magdalena Petrova | CNBC
Corning and Qualcomm rallied on Tuesday and brought a host of AI-related stocks along with them, as a pair of infrastructure deals lifted Wall Street's confidence that data center spending will remain strong. 
Chipmakers Intel and Advanced Micro Devices gained 9% and 6% respectively, while Hewlett Packard Enterprise climbed 8% and photonics company Coherent added 7%. 
All of those companies have been massive winners for investors this year, with HPE and AMD more than doubling in value and Intel almost tripling, as the artificial infrastructure buildout expands to companies beyond Nvidia . 
Corning, the glassmaker whose fiber-optic technology is becoming a key piece of AI data centers, jumped 8% on Tuesday bringing its gain for the year to 90%. The company said it's entering into a multibillion-dollar partnership with Verizon to build fiber-optic cables for AI connectivity. -
In June, Corning struck a multibillion-dollar deal with Amazon , a month after Nvidia promised to invest up to $3.2 billion in the company to build three new fiber-optic manufacturing facilities in North Carolina and Texas.
Meanwhile, Qualcomm said in a filing on Tuesday that it issued warrants to Amazon , allowing the cloud giant to acquire up to $4 billion worth of stock in the chipmaker. It's part of a pact between the two companies to build out AI infrastructure, with Amazon Web Services purchasing up to $60 billion worth of Qualcomm's server chips and other technology.
Qualcomm CFO Akash Palkhiwala said on Tuesday at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference in San Francisco that revenue from manufacturing chips for Amazon will start to be realized n the December quarter, and will be one of the "core components" in helping the company meet its $15 billion data center revenue target for fiscal 2029. 
At its investor day in June, Qualcomm said it was working with two unnamed data center companies. One of those was Amazon. Palkhiwala said Tuesday that the company is "similarly proceeding with the other data center customer."
AMD CFO Jean Hu also spoke at the Goldman event. She said that the total addressable market will now hit $3 trillion by 2030, after CEO Lisa Su said in July that the semiconductor industry would reach $2 trillion through 2028 . 
The frenzy for AI stocks comes as issues surrounding AI and data centers are at their most divisive . According to a May 2026 Gallup poll , 71% of Americans oppose data centers being built in their communities. That's translated directly into financial risk, with Anthropic poised to list negative public opinion towards AI and data centers as a risk factor in its forthcoming IPO prospectus.

Amkor Technology Announces Phase 2 of Arizona Advanced Packaging and Test Campus; Expands Investment to $12 Billion
Business Wire

AMKR

Strong customer commitments support 60,000 square meter expansion of U.S. advanced packaging capacity 
TEMPE, Ariz., September 08, 2026 --( BUSINESS WIRE )--Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR), a leading provider of outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services, today announced phase 2 of its Arizona Advanced packaging and test campus. Driven by strong customer commitments that have surpassed the 33,000 square meters of cleanroom capacity planned for phase 1, the phase 2 expansion is expected to add 60,000 square meters and bring the campus to approximately 93,000 square meters of cleanroom space. The expansion increases the project's planned investment to approximately $12 billion. 
Designed from the outset as a multi-phase project, Amkor's Arizona campus, which includes wafer bump, probe, assembly and test capabilities, is being developed to support long-term demand for advanced semiconductor packaging and test services in the U.S. Phase 2 expands manufacturing scale, and together with phase 1 is expected to support a workforce of more than 3,500 Arizona-based employees. 
"This next phase reflects the confidence our customers have placed in Amkor, the critical role advanced packaging plays in enabling the future of semiconductor innovation, and the strategic importance of our Arizona campus," said Kevin Engel, president and chief executive officer of Amkor Technology. "As chip architectures become more complex, customers need a trusted partner that can deliver at scale with the quality, technology leadership and operational discipline required for their most advanced products, and it is critical to have that capacity in the U.S." 
Amkor's Arizona campus is the first OSAT production site in the U.S. for advanced packaging in high volume, giving customers access to a full domestic turnkey manufacturing platform. Construction of phase 2 is anticipated to begin late 2027, with completion expected by the end of 2029. Amkor's Arizona 170-acre campus allows for further expansion as needed to support customer demand. 
About Amkor Technology, Inc. 
Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR) is the world's largest U.S. headquartered OSAT and is a global leader in outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services. With a strong track record of innovation, a broad and diverse geographic footprint and solid partnerships with lead customers, Amkor delivers high-quality solutions that enable the world's leading semiconductor and electronics companies to bring advanced technologies to market. The company's comprehensive portfolio includes advanced packaging, wafer-level processing, and system-in-package solutions targeting applications for smartphones, data centers, artificial intelligence, automobiles and wearables. For more information visit amkor.com .

content_text:
SCHOTT Pharma and partners replace virgin plastics in vial trays
Vidhya Edwards Munnangi 
September 8, 2026 2 min read 
SCHOTT Pharma, Takeda and Corplex have completed a full-batch shipment of pharmaceutical vials packed in trays that include recycled polypropylene, marking the move from trial work to regular operations. 
The three companies have been working on a closed-loop recycling arrangement for pharmaceutical manufacturing to balance regulatory requirements. 
During the past two years, the partners carried out risk reviews, completed production studies at ton scale, and verified that trays made with recycled material matched the assessed performance of trays produced from virgin polypropylene. 
Last month, the first full batch of vials using trays containing recycled material was sent to Takeda's manufacturing facility in Singen, Germany. 
Corplex fed the recovered material back into new tray production, while SCHOTT Pharma used the trays as intermediate packaging. 
Takeda then completed change controls and manufacturing trials, which confirmed that the trays could be processed within pharmaceutical production. 
The system can keep tray waste out of downcycling streams, incineration and landfill, while cutting dependence on fossil-based virgin polypropylene. 
It introduces recycled content into intermediate packaging at industrial scale with equivalent assessed performance. 
The closed-loop setup is linked to Scope 3, Category 1 emissions reductions across the supply chain, covering tray production by Corplex, use by SCHOTT Pharma as intermediate packaging, and shipment of vials to Takeda. 
SCHOTT Pharma is preparing to roll out the recycling model to other pharmaceutical customers in Europe. 
At present, it applies to standard packaging formats for 2R, 6R, 10R, 20R and 30R ISO vials. 
The company is continuing work on expanding the scheme, including options for paper-labelled and coloured trays. 
SCHOTT Pharma chief financial officer Reinhard Mayer said: "Moving from proof of concept to routine operations is a decisive step in commercialising circular economy approaches in pharma. 
"This first full delivery demonstrates that we can uphold the industry's uncompromising quality and patient‑safety standards while measurably improving resource efficiency and waste practice through controlled closed-loop recycling. Together with our partners, we are showing that innovation, environmental actions and compliance can reinforce one another." 
"SCHOTT Pharma and partners replace virgin plastics in vial trays" was originally created and published by Packaging Gateway , a GlobalData owned brand.

Two companies' longstanding collaboration expands into High-NA EUV and next-generation semiconductor manufacturing
Engineers at ASML inspect a High-NA EUV lithography system. (ASML) 
Samsung Electronics and Dutch manufacturer of chip equipment ASML said Tuesday they would expand their long-standing partnership on next-generation lithography technologies critical to producing advanced AI chips.
The expanded partnership between South Korea’s largest chipmaker and ASML focuses on high numerical aperture extreme ultraviolet lithography and advanced photomask solutions, areas expected to become increasingly important as chipmakers push the limits of semiconductor scaling.
As part of the expanded partnership, Samsung will help develop a next-generation 12-inch photomask platform for High-NA EUV manufacturing.
Photomasks act as templates that transfer circuit patterns onto semiconductor wafers during the chipmaking process. While the industry has traditionally relied on 6-inch photomasks, larger 12-inch formats are expected to improve manufacturing efficiency by supporting more advanced patterning processes and reducing complexity in future semiconductor production.
The move comes as global chipmakers face mounting challenges in developing smaller and more powerful semiconductors. As artificial intelligence applications drive demand for high-performance computing, companies are racing to secure technologies that can deliver greater processing capability while improving production efficiency.
High-NA EUV is widely viewed as the next major step in semiconductor lithography. The technology builds on existing EUV systems by improving resolution capabilities, allowing manufacturers to create more precise circuit patterns for future generations of logic and memory chips.
For Samsung, adopting High-NA EUV is closely tied to its competitive strategy in the memory semiconductor market. The company plans to apply the technology to future DRAM production as it seeks to strengthen its position in areas such as high-bandwidth memory, which has become a key component in AI infrastructure.
The latest cooperation also reflects a relationship between Samsung and ASML that has developed over more than a decade.
The two companies have worked closely since EUV lithography was still considered a major technological challenge for the semiconductor industry. As traditional methods approached physical limits, EUV emerged as a breakthrough technology capable of enabling more advanced semiconductor manufacturing.
ASML, the world’s leading supplier of semiconductor lithography equipment, has become a critical player in the global chip supply chain through its EUV systems. The company remains the only manufacturer capable of supplying commercial EUV lithography machines used by leading semiconductor producers worldwide.
Samsung was among the early semiconductor companies to adopt EUV technology and has continued expanding its use across both memory and foundry operations. The company’s experience with EUV manufacturing has positioned it as one of the key players in the transition toward next-generation semiconductor processes.
"The AI era is transforming the semiconductor industry and increasing the importance of technological innovation across the entire value chain," Samsung Electronics Vice Chairman and CEO Jun Young-hyun said. "By further strengthening our collaboration with ASML, we are helping lay the foundation for the next generation of AI and semiconductor innovation."
ASML President and CEO Christophe Fouquet also emphasized the importance of cooperation between equipment suppliers and chip manufacturers as the semiconductor industry enters a new phase of technological competition.
"As the industry enters a new era driven by artificial intelligence, close collaboration with our customers becomes even more important," Fouquet said.
The partnership highlights a broader shift in the semiconductor industry, where access to advanced manufacturing technologies has become a strategic advantage. As demand for AI-related chips continues to reshape the market, Samsung and ASML are seeking to strengthen their positions by advancing the technologies that will define the next generation of semiconductor production.

Moderna and Merck’s mRNA success fuels focus on ‘scaling out and scaling down’
September 8, 2026  |  
2 min read  |  
Nick Paul Taylor 
Twitter 
LinkedIn 
Facebook 
Email
Print
iStock, Christoph Burgstedt 
After mastering mass-market mRNA production during the pandemic, the industry now needs to achieve the timely delivery of individualized vaccines to thousands of patients.
The recent clinical success of Merck and Moderna’s intismeran autogene raised expectations for personalized mRNA cancer vaccines across the industry. Yet getting the products to patients presents new challenges.
In the past, the industry was focused on scaling up, Roberta Duncan, founder and principal of strategic consulting firm The Modeste Duncan Group, told BioSpace . Now, the conversation is about “scaling out and scaling down,” added Duncan, who also serves on the board of the Alliance for mRNA Medicines.
To make intismeran, Moderna sequences an individual’s cancer and healthy cells and analyzes the data using an automated bioinformatics system to identify up to 34 patient-specific neoantigens. Formulated in a lipid nanoparticle delivery system, mRNA encoding the neoantigens triggers protein production in the body to drive an immune response against the tumor.
By 2025, Moderna had reduced the time from sample collection to vaccine administration to around six weeks, down from roughly seven to eight weeks in 2019 . The turnaround time “can probably be brought under one month,” Guggenheim Securities analysts said in an Aug. 21 note to investors, citing Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center computational oncologist Benjamin Greenbaum.
Moderna has set up a dedicated facility in Massachusetts to support intismeran’s planned launch. The company calculates that the facility can support the vaccine “for several years,” Moderna President Stephen Hoge said on an earnings call in July. The plant should “satisfy the initial indication” of melanoma, Hoge added, and Moderna will add more capacity to meet demand beyond an initial launch.
Hoge was speaking before the INTerpath-001 trial readout raised expectations for intismeran. Last month, an earlier-than-expected trial readout showed the personalized vaccine combined with Keytruda improved outcomes in patients with melanoma, nearly doubling Moderna’s share price while Merck’s stock jumped 12% .
Cancer 
Moderna stock nearly doubles as Merck-partnered mRNA cancer vaccine meets Phase 3 goal 
Melanoma was slower to recur in patients receiving Merck and Moderna’s mRNA vaccine with Keytruda, supporting use of the combination in adjuvant treatment. The partners plan to take the data to the FDA.
August 19, 2026
 ·  3 min read
 ·  Nick Paul Taylor 
Read more 
Moderna, which is primarily responsible for manufacturing intismeran under the terms of its deal with Merck, did not respond to BioSpace ’s questions about how the clinical success has affected the company’s thinking about demand and capacity.
Moderna’s ability to make intismeran for the thousands of patients in active trials of the vaccine is built on years of investment in in-house capabilities. Biotechs without such capabilities can supply the market by working with CDMOs, Duncan said, provided they can find partners “willing to invest in miniaturizing scale, because they’re all built for large-scale manufacturing.”
As personalized mRNA vaccines come to market, Duncan warned, “we’re going to have to have a really hard conversation about cost of goods and the cost of manufacturing.” Believing that clinical data show the novel modality works, Duncan now sees the speed and cost of production as the keys to commercial success.
“It’s not going to be on the biology,” she said. “It’s going to be on the logistics and the cost.”
Editor’s note: Heather McKenzie contributed reporting to this story.

AI-designed bespoke mRNA therapy reduces melanoma recurrence, metastasis, and death 
Merck and Moderna’s Phase III clinical trial demonstrates the effectiveness of bespoke mRNA therapy, hinting at potential treatments for other cancers.
Søren Hough , Editor, Drug Modalities September 7, 2026
schedule 10 Min Read 
Unsplash/okeykat 
link 
When Katalin Karikó began her work on mRNA technology , her first idea wasn’t to create a vaccine – it was to treat disease. A few years, a pandemic, and one Nobel Prize later, a late-stage human trial has finally confirmed that mRNA can be given to patients as a therapeutic. 
Last month, Moderna and Merck & Co. (known as MSD outside of North America) announced positive results from its Phase III INTerpath-001 trial ( NCT05933577 ). The study investigated the efficacy of Moderna’s mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (LNP) therapeutic intismeran autogene (also known as mRNA-4157 or V940) in combination with Merck’s checkpoint inhibitor antibody, pembrolizumab (Keytruda). The unpublished results suggest that the two-pronged approach dramatically improved treatment and survival when compared with the antibody alone. 
This positive signal for an mRNA therapeutic could portend a sea change in cancer treatment. This is the first mRNA immunotherapy to pass the final hurdle of a Phase III clinical trial. Intismeran is also the first bespoke (patient-specific) cancer immunotherapy that has a chance of receiving regulatory approval – a level of customization made possible by Moderna’s artificial intelligence (AI) algorithm. The combination of these emerging technologies raises important questions about their design and regulation. 
Related: MHRA unleashes guidance on mRNA immunotherapies 
For this two-part story , BioXconomy reached out to a range of experts, from the primary investigators studying intismeran to external scholars researching the role of machine learning and AI in drug design. We found that their general sentiment is excitement at what these Phase III results could mean for addressing other forms of cancer. Not everyone is sold just yet – but even the most careful scientists we spoke to remain cautiously optimistic. 
“Landmark moment” 
INTerpath-001 divided over 1,100 trial participants with Stagead IIB–IV cutaneous melanoma into two groups. The first group received pembrolizumab alone, while the other received the antibody alongside intismeran. The trial was set to run for approximately one year with the proviso that dosing would end if the patients experienced “unacceptable toxicity” following treatment. 
The team found that the combination of intismeran and pembrolizumab offered a dramatic improvement on preventing metastasis, recurrence, and death in patients compared to the antibody on its own. The researchers noted in their press release that they saw no new safety indications – for example, severe adverse reactions – relative to the baseline set by previous intismeran trials. 
Related: First mRNA cancer vaccines a paradigm shift for treatment 
Georgina Long, professor, director, and medical oncologist at the Melanoma Institute Australia, was the lead investigator on INTerpath-001. 
“This is the first Phase III study to show that intismeran, a treatment based on the unique mutational ‘fingerprint’ of a patient’s own tumor, given in combination with pembrolizumab, can reduce the risk of recurrence or death in patients with completely resected stage IIB–IV melanoma compared to pembrolizumab alone,” she shared with us in a statement. “Intismeran, in combination with pembrolizumab, has the potential to establish a new treatment paradigm in the adjuvant melanoma setting, helping patients remain cancer-free for longer.” 
A Melanoma Institute spokesperson called the trial results a “landmark moment” in melanoma care. They added that Long and the team at the Melanoma Institute are looking forward to the full Phase III trials being published. They said this data will be shared “at a congress later this year.” 
The positive results of this Phase III trial build on a Phase IIb trial called KEYNOTE-942 ( NCT03897881 ). That study yielded similarly promising data earlier this year: pembrolizumab plus intismeran led to a 59% reduction in distant melanoma metastasis or death and a 49% reduction in recurrence or death when compared to the antibody by itself. 
Related: Moderna trial suggests mRNA vaccine may halt solid tumor growth 
For lead investigator Adnan Khattak, medical oncologist at One Clinical Research and Edith Cowan University in Australia, those numbers were only part of a much bigger story. 
“For me, the most important aspect of KEYNOTE-942 was not simply the magnitude of the clinical result, but the proof of principle,” Khattak told BioXconomy . “For the first time, we have seen a personalized immune-modulating approach – an individualized neoantigen therapy [INT] combined with checkpoint inhibition – demonstrate meaningful improvement in outcomes in patients with high-risk resected melanoma.” 
“That is conceptually very important,” he continued. “Rather than giving every patient an identical immune therapy, we are effectively providing the immune system with information derived from that patient's own tumor and attempting to direct immunity toward those tumor-specific targets.” 
Dusting for fingerprINTs 
mRNA-based immunotherapies are often referred to as “vaccines” in the press and even by drug developers due to their role promoting an immune response in the patient. Yet some organizations have pushed back against the term. For example, UK regulators stated in 2025 that “individualized mRNA cancer immunotherapies do not meet the definition of vaccines” because they treat disease rather than prevent it. 
Moderna and Merck also avoided using the term in their press release. A Merck spokesperson clarified their choice of terminology to BioXconomy . 
“Intismeran is a therapeutic vaccine, not a prophylactic vaccine,” the spokesperson said. “Unlike preventive vaccines, intismeran is designed to address an existing clinical challenge by activating tumor-specific immune responses after cancer has already been diagnosed.” 
The decision to use the term “individualized neoantigen therapy (INT)” over “therapeutic vaccine” is intended to emphasize the bespoke nature of intismeran. 
“We use the term INT because it better reflects what makes this approach unique. Rather than taking a one-size-fits-all approach, INTs are designed around the unique mutational signature found in an individual patient's tumor.” 
That means each patient needs their cancerous tissue extracted and analyzed so that it can be used to design an mRNA-LNP formulation that fits their needs. 
“Intismeran is designed using a patient’s tumor sample to identify the unique mutational signature, or ‘fingerprint,’ of their cancer,” the spokesperson explained. “This information is then used to create a personalized synthetic mRNA coding for up to 34 neoantigens – abnormal proteins that arise from mutations in cancer cells and are not found in healthy cells.” 
“Since these tumor-specific mutations are unique to each individual, they could create a personalized therapy tailored to generate anti-cancer immunity.” 
This precision medicine approach is what excites Khattak, who believes classical cancer therapeutics are too broad-brush to address the disease effectively. 
“Many of our systemic cancer treatments remain relatively generic,” he told us. “Chemotherapy, and to a considerable extent immunotherapy, are administered according to tumor type and stage rather than being individually designed for a particular patient's cancer.” 
His point echoes sentiments we’ve heard from other industry leaders about the drawbacks of chemotherapy: the nonspecific side effects are potentially life-altering . 
“The direction we need to move toward is the right treatment for the right patient at the right time, rather than a one-size-fits-all approach.” 
Researchers have begun to explore how to generate personalized mRNA-LNP therapies for use in the clinic, for example in the realm of genome editing . 
“We have already made substantial progress with personalized targeted therapies, where treatment is selected according to specific molecular alterations,” Khattak continued. “What has historically been much more difficult is developing a truly personalized immune-modulating therapy.” 
mRNA-based cancer therapeutics are advancing across the world. BioXconomy has covered how these medicines are being tested against late-stage lung cancer , pancreatic cancer , and solid tumors . 
“Individualized neoantigen therapy represents an important step in that direction,” said Khattak. “The treatment is designed around the unique mutational and neoantigen profile of an individual patient's tumor, with the aim of generating a tumor-specific immune response. The encouraging results from KEYNOTE-942, and now the subsequent Phase III program, suggest that this concept can translate into clinically meaningful benefit.” 
Resource cost 
Bespoke cancer drugs like intismeran could shift paradigms around cancer treatment and give hope to patients who have run out of other options. However, what the drug gains in customization could also make it an expensive medicine to produce, with potential consequences for patient access. 
“These therapies are inherently resource intensive,” Khattak confirmed. “They require tumor sequencing, sophisticated computational analysis, selection of patient-specific neoantigens, individualized manufacturing, quality assurance, and rapid delivery back to the treating center. I would therefore expect the initial costs to be substantial.” 
Still, he believes it’s premature to think about pricing. “It is difficult to predict the eventual cost at this stage, as pricing will ultimately be determined by the sponsors and the healthcare systems in which these treatments are introduced.” 
The Merck spokesperson agreed. 
“It’s too early at this stage to comment on pricing or access,” the Merck spokesperson said. “MSD has had a long history of responsibly pricing medicines and vaccines to reflect their value to patients, payers, and society, and we plan to continue to uphold this commitment for any pipeline asset that may come to market in the future.” 
Khattak believes that even a high price may be warranted given the typical costs of cancer treatment for the patient and the wider healthcare system. 
“The key question should ultimately be value rather than acquisition cost alone,” Khattak said. “We will need robust health-economic and cost-benefit analyses incorporating not only the price of manufacturing the therapy but also the potential value of preventing recurrence, metastatic disease, and subsequent lines of treatment.” 
Looking ahead 
There is still more information to come on the Phase III trial once it has undergone peer review. But if the data bears out, Khattak believes mRNA-based INTs could find applications in other cancer types. 
“I think the broader significance extends well beyond melanoma,” he said. “Individualized neoantigen therapies are being investigated across a range of tumor types, and we hope that ongoing studies will reproduce the encouraging results seen in melanoma.” 
Researchers like Khattak envision a world where medicines aren’t designed against common denominator mutations but rather the precise variants found in patient tumors. 
“For decades, personalized oncology has largely meant matching molecularly targeted drugs to particular genomic abnormalities,” he continued. “We may now be entering an era in which we can also personalize the immune response itself.” 
“If these results continue to be confirmed across Phase III studies and other cancers, this could represent an important shift in how we think about cancer treatment – from treating a tumor category to increasingly treating the unique biology of an individual patient's tumor.” 
Not everyone is as optimistic about the future of mRNA tech. Jared Auclair and Rominder Singh, both of whom serve on faculty at Northeastern University in Boston and who study emerging technologies in drug development, are waiting to see more data. Neither were involved in the development or testing of intismeran. 
“Moderna and Merck's melanoma results represent real progress, but we don't read them as proof that mRNA cancer vaccines work broadly,” Auclair and Singh shared with BioXconomy . “A search of ClinicalTrials.gov shows 32 active mRNA cancer vaccine studies, and to date only one has produced a clear positive result.” 
For Auclair and Singh, this stagnation runs up against a broader context of mRNA medicines that have been unable to make headway in the clinic. 
“Just a few days after the Moderna results, BioNTech and Genentech terminated their colorectal cancer vaccine trial, and Moderna's own CMV vaccine failed in Phase III last October,” they said. “The experts believe that the differing outcomes come down to tumor biology and trial design, not the mRNA platform itself where melanoma is immunologically ‘hot’ and responds well to immunotherapy while colorectal cancer is ‘cold’ and has historically resisted it.” 
For now, Auclair and Singh are keeping an open mind as to whether the tide could turn on the tech. 
“We see mRNA as a promising delivery chassis, but with 32 shots on goal and only one scored so far, time will tell whether that one success translates into a broader pattern or stays an outlier.” 
Quotes have been lightly edited for clarity. This article was updated on September 7, 2026, to update Adnan Khattak's affiliation. Click here to read the second part of this story.

title: Moderna advances mRNA cancer push, eyes in vivo CAR-T and Korea trials - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz

content_text:
Moderna advances mRNA cancer push, eyes in vivo CAR-T and Korea trials 
Moderna pursues vaccine-only cancer strategies, preps in vivo CAR-T and Korea clinical studies while advancing norovirus and targeted mRNA therapies 
입력 2026.09.07. 06:01 업데이트 2026.09.07. 08:30 
조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 
U.S. drugmaker Moderna is expanding its cancer drug development following the phase 3 success of its personalized messenger RNA (mRNA) cancer vaccine.
Beyond combination therapy with immunotherapy, the company is evaluating the potential for a vaccine-only regimen and is expected to broaden its research to "in vivo chimeric antigen receptor T cells (CAR-T)," which kill cancer cells directly in the body with a single injection.
A staged photo shows a syringe and needle placed in front of the Moderna logo of a U.S. pharmaceutical company. /Courtesy of Reuters Yonhap 
On the 7th, according to the pharmaceutical and biotech industry, Moderna is developing a range of mRNA-based cancer vaccines and therapies. Its personalized cancer vaccine "intismeran autogene," which recently delivered phase 3 results in combination with Merck's (MSD) immunotherapy Keytruda, is also undergoing additional studies, including a monotherapy approach.
Kim Hee-su, vice president at Moderna Korea, said, "In addition to the combination therapy co-developed with MSD, we are looking at the potential for intismeran autogene as a monotherapy," and added, "Preclinical studies are underway, and we expect to enter full-scale clinical trials around the end of next year."
The intismeran autogene and Keytruda combination therapy, whose clinical results were released in the previous month, met its primary endpoint of suppressing cancer recurrence and metastasis in a phase 3 trial in high-risk melanoma patients. This is the first time an mRNA-based cancer vaccine has met primary endpoints in a phase 3 trial.
Intismeran autogene is made as a patient-specific therapy by analyzing mutations unique to cancer cells from a patient's tumor tissue and selecting neoantigens likely to elicit an immune response.
Currently, MSD is leading the development of combination therapy, including late-stage trials. In Korea, MSD has completed enrollment of melanoma patients for late-stage trials and is conducting the study.
Building on these clinical results, Moderna plans to broaden the use of mRNA in cancer treatment beyond personalized cancer vaccines.
A representative area is "in vivo CAR-T," a next-generation CAR-T technology that kills cancer cells directly in the body with a single injection. By delivering RNA to specific immune cells to generate CAR-T cells inside the patient, it is considered a next-generation technology that could significantly change the manufacturing process of existing cell therapies.
Kim said, "If mRNA is applied to in vivo CAR-T, it could change the complex manufacturing steps of existing cell therapies," adding, "If we can reduce the process of harvesting a patient's cells, manipulating and culturing them externally, and reinfusing them, and instead induce immune cell function directly in the body, this could evolve into a new treatment approach."
The company is also developing mRNA therapies that target antigens commonly found in specific cancer patient groups. Its core candidate, "mRNA-4359," is in phase 2 as both a Keytruda combination and a monotherapy in melanoma and Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients. In phase 1/2 results released in April, it showed a meaningful antitumor response as a first-line treatment for advanced or metastatic melanoma.
While expanding the scope of its mRNA platform in oncology, Moderna is also seeking new growth drivers in infectious disease vaccines. A key next program is the norovirus vaccine.
Norovirus is a major infectious disease that causes vomiting and diarrhea, especially in winter, but vaccine development is considered difficult due to the virus's diversity and frequent mutations. Several corporations have attempted to develop vaccines in the past but fell short in clinical trials. Moderna is currently conducting late-stage clinical trials for its norovirus vaccine.
Moderna emphasizes that for its core business, the COVID-19 vaccine, it must maintain a stable vaccination base focused on older adults and high-risk groups.
As perceptions of COVID-19 as a cold-like illness spread recently, vaccination rates remain lower than for influenza. According to the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency, the budget for procuring next year's COVID-19 vaccines has decreased by about 10% from this year, and the procurement volume has also fallen by about 500,000 doses.
Kim said, "COVID-19 remains a significant respiratory infectious disease that can lead to hospitalization and death among older adults, so regular vaccination is needed for high-risk groups, including older adults and those with weakened immunity," adding, "As the older population grows, we must guarantee sufficient vaccination opportunities for high-risk groups when needed."

BASF has officially inaugurated a fully modernised production plant for acid chlorides and chloroformates at its Ludwigshafen site. The investment increases production capacity by around 30 % and reduces the product carbon footprint by an average of 19 %, with applications spanning coatings, pharmaceuticals, and crop protection.

Source: BASF 
Advertisement:
BASF has officially inaugurated its fully modernised plant for the production of acid chlorides and chloroformates at its Ludwigshafen Verbund site in Germany. The investment, amounting to a low three-digit million-euro sum, represents a significant upgrade of the production infrastructure and increases capacity at the site by approximately 30 %. BASF states it is one of the world’s leading manufacturers of these products, with production facilities in Ludwigshafen and Yeosu, South Korea. 
The modernised plant is designed to combine increased production capacity with improved sustainability performance and long-term supply reliability for customers worldwide. Since 2025, BASF has produced its entire Ludwigshafen portfolio of around 25 acid chlorides and chloroformates using renewable electricity credits, covering all upstream raw material processes. This transition has reduced the portfolio’s product carbon footprint by an average of 19 %, without changes to product specifications, certifications, or ordering processes. 
Coatings among key application areas for expanded production 
Acid chlorides and chloroformates serve as essential chemical building blocks across a wide range of value chains. Customers use them in applications including pharmaceuticals, crop protection products, organic peroxides, coatings, plastics, and rubber mixtures. The expanded capacity is intended to help BASF meet growing global demand whilst ensuring reliable supply of these intermediates. 
Mary Kurian, Member of the Board of Executive Directors of BASF SE, commented on the inauguration: “The opening of this modernized plant demonstrates BASF’s commitment to investing in competitive and sustainable production assets at our Ludwigshafen Verbund site and in Europe. By combining increased capacity, supply reliability and a significantly reduced product carbon footprint, we are creating value for our customers and supporting their green transformation.” 
Sustainability strategy and Scope 3 emission reductions 
The use of renewable electricity credits supports customers in advancing their Scope 3 emission-reduction efforts, a factor of increasing relevance across the coatings and chemicals supply chain. BASF emphasises that the transition requires no adjustments to product specifications, certifications, or ordering processes on the part of customers. 
Ketan Joshi, President of BASF’s Intermediates division, added: “This investment strengthens our position as one of the world’s leading suppliers of acid chlorides and chloroformates and supports our vision of being the preferred partner for sustainable intermediates. The modernized plant further supports our ability to provide reliable supply and consistent quality to customers around the world who depend on these essential intermediates.”

title: EVG Supports CPO Production With Advanced Bonding, NIL - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media
source: Google News: THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media
publisher: THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media
query: ("EVG" OR "EV Group") ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-09-01 before:2026-10-01
content_text:
EVG's NILPhotonics Competence Center. (Photo: EVG) 
EV Group (EVG) said on Sept. 2 it is accelerating customers' mass production of co-packaged optics (CPO) through its technology and infrastructure.
"CPO requires comprehensive process expertise because it integrates photonic and electronic components using advanced packaging technologies," said Bernd Dielacher, director of business development at EVG. "With decades of accumulated expertise and close collaboration, EVG is helping customers develop and optimize the entire manufacturing process from early CPO development through high-volume manufacturing (HVM)." CPO has recently drawn attention for large-scale data centers, AI infrastructure and high-performance computing (HPC).
EVG has several bonding technologies for CPO as well as nanoimprint lithography (NIL). Its fusion bonding technology bonds surfaces using dielectric materials alone and is used for heterogeneous integration of next-generation optical modulation materials such as thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) and barium titanate (BTO). It can also heterogeneously integrate light-emitting III-V compound semiconductors to create laser sources.
Hybrid bonding is an advanced packaging technology that directly connects copper (Cu) surfaces when stacking and interconnecting two semiconductor chips, or dies. It can minimize parasitic effects between photonic integrated circuits (PICs) and electronic integrated circuits (EICs) while enabling high-density integration. Parasitic effects interfere with signal flow at bonding interfaces and cause transmission losses. The technology is suited for high-bandwidth products.
EVG also has oxide-free room-temperature bonding technology. It enables low-loss, optically transparent interfaces and integrates heat-spreader materials such as diamond and silicon carbide (SiC) to efficiently transfer heat through interfaces.
NIL is a manufacturing technology capable of precisely producing nanoscale optical devices or circuit patterns in high volumes. It directly transfers circuit patterns by pressing a mold, or stamp, containing a specific semiconductor circuit pattern onto a substrate. The process is simpler and less expensive than deep ultraviolet (DUV) and extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography. Lithography equipment typically uses a light source and photomask to create fine circuit patterns.
NIL is useful for manufacturing CPO grating couplers, vertical light and beam-shaping components, and lenses and components for micro light-emitting diode (LED) packaging. Grating couplers are fine-patterned structures that help light efficiently enter and exit between chips or between a chip and an optical fiber.
EVG's NILPhotonics Competence Center is a process development platform that works with customers to enable faster and easier adoption of NIL technology for CPO development. It provides consulting across CPO processes as well as technology and equipment solutions. In particular, it provides contract manufacturing of large-area step-and-repeat (S&R) master stamps required for NIL processes and replicated stamps used for actual printing. Their availability in high volumes at low cost makes it easier to scale up production.
EVG also operates a Heterogeneous Integration Competence Center. Customers can test EVG equipment and receive services to optimize next-generation processes. The center supports areas requiring more advanced system integration, including HPC, data centers and CPO.
EVG expects the industry to shift from CPO toward optical input/output (I/O) chiplet architectures and advanced 3D photonic-electronic integration (EI). CPO horizontally places PICs, light sources, micro-optical structures and computing chips on a single package substrate. Optical I/O chiplet architectures combine optical interconnect functions as modules. Advanced 3D photonic-EI vertically stacks PICs and EICs.
"With our semiconductor 3D and heterogeneous integration technologies and capabilities, we can support not only CPO implementation but also optical I/O architectures," EVG said. "We will expand semiconductor packaging technology into next-generation photonic-EI systems."

GeoCue Elevates Survey-Grade Drone Mapping with Ouster's BABA-Compliant Native Color Rev8 Digital Lidar
Provided by Business Wire Sep 2, 2026, 4:00:00 PM 
GeoCue Elevates Survey-Grade Drone Mapping with Ouster's BABA-Compliant Native Color Rev8 Digital Lidar 
Pairing survey-grade precision with Ouster’s 256-channel Rev8 OS1 Max lidar, GeoCue’s latest TrueView lineup sets a new benchmark for U.S. drone surveying 
Ouster, Inc. (Nasdaq: OUST) (“Ouster” or the “Company”), a leader in sensing and perception for Physical AI, announced a strategic partnership with GeoCue, a premier provider of drone mapping payloads and software, to integrate Ouster’s native color Rev8 OS1 Max digital lidar into GeoCue’s TrueView product line. The collaboration pairs GeoCue's TrueView 1 payloads and LP360 software with Ouster's digital lidar to deliver survey-grade data to the utility and infrastructure industries.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260902576177/en/ 
Ouster Rev8 OS1 Max on GeoCue's TrueView drone payload, mapping a construction site (product rendering).
GeoCue is expanding its TrueView lineup to include options featuring the Ouster Rev8 OS1 Max, which is Build America, Buy America Act (BABA)-compliant. These new options give customers who have domestic production requirements a high-performance solution without technical compromises.
Ouster and GeoCue selected the Rev8 OS1 Max after joint flight testing and firmware tuning in Huntsville, Alabama. "We are moving America's drone surveying onto American sensing by pairing our TrueView payloads with Ouster's Rev8 OS1 Max," said Frank Darmayan, CEO of GeoCue. "This transition allows us to offer our customers a compliant, high-performance solution that delivers the survey-grade data they depend on for critical infrastructure monitoring and large-scale mapping projects."
The Rev8 OS1 Max brings four key advantages to GeoCue's utility and infrastructure customers:
Superior Precision: A smaller spot size and tighter beam allow TrueView payloads to resolve thin objects such as power lines and structural edges.
Expanded Operational Range: Longer range (200m at 10% reflectivity) clears altitude restrictions around utility corridors, letting operators fly higher while maintaining data quality.
Native Color Integration: The Rev8 OS1 Max captures native color in addition to 3D lidar data, so every point arrives inherently aligned to its color. Alongside the dual cameras in every TrueView payload, that gives LP360 an additional RGB reference for registering camera imagery to the point cloud, enabling tighter sensor fusion.
Density at Speed: 256 channels in 2K and 4K modes keep point density high even at fast flight speeds, supporting long-corridor surveys by propeller and fixed-wing aircraft.
"Our partnership with GeoCue is a testament to how native color digital lidar can serve as the bedrock for physical AI applications that have a profound impact on infrastructure and public safety," said Ouster CEO Angus Pacala. "By integrating our Rev8 OS1 Max sensor, we are providing the survey-grade precision and reliability required to empower the next generation of drone mapping professionals."
Experience the Rev8 OS1 Max for Drone Surveying at Commercial UAV Expo 
Ouster will be showcasing its Rev8 OS1 Max native color digital lidar at Booth #1653 during the Commercial UAV Expo in Las Vegas (September 1-3, 2026). Attendees can stop by the booth for live hardware demonstrations or schedule a meeting with our technical team.
About Ouster 
Ouster (Nasdaq: OUST) is a leader in sensing and perception for Physical AI across industrial, robotics, automotive, and smart infrastructure. With a unified platform of high-performance digital lidar, cameras, AI compute, sensor fusion and perception software, and AI models, Ouster delivers solutions that improve quality of life in the physical world. Headquartered in San Francisco, CA, Ouster has a global presence serving thousands of customers with offices in the Americas, Europe, and Asia-Pacific. For more information about our products, visit www.ouster.com , contact our sales team , or connect with us on X or LinkedIn .
About GeoCue 
GeoCue brings geospatial professionals advanced drone, mobile and terrestrial surveying equipment, point-cloud processing software, workflows, training and support for high-accuracy LiDAR and imagery mapping. With TrueView LiDAR and imaging sensors and LP360 point-cloud processing software, GeoCue provides complete solutions for successful data collection, processing, quality control and deliverable creation. GeoCue meets customers where they are in terms of technology, adoption, budget and resources while supporting their continued growth. To learn more about GeoCue, visit www.geocue.com .

National Wealth Fund backs Nexeon’s sodium battery tech with £53 million 
The money brings the Oxfordshire-based company’s latest investment round to £100 million (US$133 million), with additional investments from the Korea Development Bank and Honda Xcelerator Ventures.
Will Norman , Senior Reporter , Informa September 2, 2026
schedule 2 Min Read 
Nexeon claims that its technology enables faster charging and higher energy density in battery systems, with a variety of applications including electric vehicles. Image: Nexeon 
The UK National Wealth Fund has invested £52.6 million (US$70 million) into silicon anode battery technology startup Nexeon. 
The money brings the Oxfordshire-based company’s latest investment round to £100 million (US$133 million), with additional investments from the Korea Development Bank and Honda Xcelerator Ventures. 
The National Wealth Fund said the investment supports Nexeon’s “continued scale-up and commercialisation activities”. The funds will go towards Nexeon’s plans for a pilot UK manufacturing facility and its ongoing research and development (R&D) efforts. 
Nexeon is developing silicon anode technology for energy storage systems, which it said can enable the production of higher energy density lithium-ion batteries. The company operates a mass production facility in South Korea and has a research base in Japan, as well as its Oxfordshire headquarters. 
Nexeon claims that its technology enables faster charging and higher energy density in battery systems, with a variety of applications including electric vehicles (EVs). 
Related: Foresight invests in 40GWh LDES cap-and-floor winning pumped hydro project in Scotland 
"Companies like Nexeon show the strength of British innovation,” said chancellor of the exchequer John Healey. “And if we are serious about growth, we must be serious about backing British businesses like this with conditions for them to start, scale and succeed here in the UK, as the National Wealth Fund are doing here.” 
Oliver Holbourn, chief executive officer of the National Wealth Fund, added: “Our investment in Nexeon is fully aligned with our mission to support clean energy innovation and economic growth. Backing advanced battery technology is key to building a globally competitive EV supply chain in the UK”. 
Scott Brown, chief executive of Nexeon, said the investment was a “strong endorsement of Nexeon’s technology and our role in enabling the next generation of lithium-ion batteries”. 
Back in January, the National Wealth Fund revealed plans to facilitate £100 million of investment into UK clean energy , prioritising battery manufacturing and energy storage alongside grid upgrades and carbon capture projects. 
Industries minister Blair McDougall said: "Hot on the heels of a £130 million investment into net zero vehicle technologies, our Modern Industrial Strategy is doubling down on frontier industries like batteries to help businesses like Nexeon grow their business, create skilled jobs and drive good growth right across the UK.” 
There have also been some efforts to onshore solar supply and manufacturing in the UK. Great British Energy invested in Naked Energy , a solar thermal company, last month.

ABB closes Hoglund acquisition 
WorkBoat Staff 
News 
Technology 
Business 
SHARE 
From left: Peter Morsbach, Hoglund CEO; Saara Kuusisto, global business line manager, marine systems, ABB’s Marine & Ports division; and Rune Braastad, president, ABB’s Marine & Ports division. Hoglund photo. 
ABB has completed its acquisition of Norwegian marine automation specialist Hoglund AS, the companies announced.
ABB has completed its acquisition of Norwegian marine automation specialist Hoglund AS, the companies announced Wednesday.
The transaction closed Sept. 1, roughly two months after the two sides announced the agreement on June 26. ABB said at the time that the deal was expected to close in the third quarter of 2026, subject to customary regulatory approvals. Financial terms were not disclosed.
The purchase covers Hoglund's global operations and its 85 employees in Norway, Poland, Romania and China. Hoglund, which is headquartered in Tonsberg, will be folded into ABB's Marine & Ports division. The company was previously owned by Eitzen Group .
At the center of the deal is Hoglund's Integrated Automation System, a modular and scalable platform now installed aboard more than 600 ships. The system pulls together data from engines, generators, and cargo systems to support safety, energy efficiency, and operational performance.
The IAS is built on ABB's own control system hardware, specifically ABB's 800M and S800 platforms, according to the companies' June announcement.
"By adding Hoglund's automation platform as a solution to ABB's product portfolio, we combine advanced marine automation capabilities with global reach and an extensive service network, creating a powerful competitive advantage," said Rune Braastad, president of ABB's Marine & Ports division. "This gives us the opportunity to grow our automation portfolio, address a wider range of vessel types, and serve their evolving needs even better than before. I'm delighted to welcome our new colleagues from Hoglund. Together, we will drive innovation and create lasting value for shipowners, operators, and yards."
"For me, today marks a recognition of the automation technology, expertise, and experience we have built at Hoglund over the past 30 years," said Hoglund CEO Peter Morsbach. "As we take our next steps together as part of ABB, I am excited to build on the strengths of Hoglund and ABB together, advancing marine automation for the benefit of customers worldwide."
Saara Kuusisto, global business line manager for marine systems in ABB's Marine & Ports division, said the combined operation would broaden what the company can offer shipowners.
"Together, we will strengthen our automation expertise and expand our capabilities to deliver even more comprehensive integrated solutions to ships worldwide," Kuusisto said. "We will build on Hoglund's distinctive values while continuing to focus on what matters most to our customers."

content_text:
Nexeon raises £100m as National Wealth Fund invests
Abingdon firm is developing silicon anode materials which will help to reduce charging times and extend range of electric vehicles
Share: 
Listen to article 
EnviroTech Investment Manufacturing Battery startup Nexeon has secured backing from the National Wealth Fund as part of a £100 million funding round. 
The National Wealth Fund has committed £52.6m, with other new investors in the round including the Korea Development Bank and Honda Xcelerator Ventures. 
Nexeon, headquartered in Abingdon near Oxford, is developing silicon anode materials which enable production of higher energy density lithium-ion batteries, helping to reduce charging times and extend the range of electric vehicles. 
The investment round supports the company’s continued scale-up and commercialisation activities and marks another key milestone in the pathway to high-volume manufacturing and global customer adoption. 
The National Wealth Fund’s financing will support Nexeon’s development of a UK-based pilot manufacturing facility, directly supporting their research and development activities and allowing the expansion of its advanced manufacturing technology unit, creating a number of new highly skilled jobs. 
By investing in innovative battery technologies and expanding local manufacturing capacity, the Fund says its investment will help to decarbonise supply chains, boost place-based investment and strengthen sovereign capabilities — supporting all three of the National Wealth Fund’s strategic ambitions. 
Honda Xcelerator Ventures is the global open innovation program of the Honda Motor Co. Ltd., and invests in technologies shaping the future of mobility and electrification. The Korea Development Bank is a leading policy bank in South Korea, focused on supporting industrial innovation and global expansion of Korean-linked manufacturing ecosystems. 
£100m competition backs British AI firms to fix public services 
Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey MP said: “Companies like Nexeon show the strength of British innovation. And if we are serious about growth, we must be serious about backing British businesses like this with conditions for them to start, scale and succeed here in the UK, as the National Wealth Fund are doing here. That’s how we’ll get good growth and jobs in every postcode.” 
Oliver Holbourn, CEO of the National Wealth Fund, said: “Our investment in Nexeon is fully aligned with our mission to support clean energy innovation and economic growth. Backing advanced battery technology is key to building a globally competitive EV supply chain in the UK, as the thought-leadership paper we recently published identifies. 
“This investment will help unlock private capital, support high-value jobs and drive regional growth, while helping to position the UK at the forefront of innovation in the battery sector.” 
Dr Scott Brown (pictured), CEO of Nexeon, said: “This investment is a strong endorsement of Nexeon’s technology and our role in enabling the next generation of lithium-ion batteries. The National Wealth Fund’s support reflects the strategic importance of our work, not only in advancing battery performance but also in strengthening the UK’s position in the global battery supply chain.” 
David Lamb, CFO at Nexeon, added: “We continue to strengthen our shareholder register with the addition of the Korea Development Bank, Honda and the National Wealth Fund. The quality of the Nexeon commercial proposition is reflected in the quality of investors we continue to attract.”

ABB completes acquisition of Høglund to expand marine automation offering
Web story
ABB has finalized its acquisition of marine automation specialist Høglund AS headquartered in Tønsberg, Norway. The transaction was completed September 1st 2026, following the announcement of the agreement published on June 26th.
Complementing ABB’s existing marine automation offering and supporting growth across a wide range of vessel segments, the newly acquired business includes Høglund’s global operations, with a total of 85 employees in Norway, Poland, Romania, and China.
“By adding Høglund’s automation platform as a solution to ABB’s product portfolio, we combine advanced marine automation capabilities with global reach and an extensive service network, creating a powerful competitive advantage,” said Rune Braastad, President, ABB’s Marine & Ports division. “This gives us the opportunity to grow our automation portfolio, address a wider range of vessel types, and serve their evolving needs even better than before. I’m delighted to welcome our new colleagues from Høglund. Together, we will drive innovation and create lasting value for shipowners, operators, and yards.”
“For me, today marks a recognition of the automation technology, expertise, and experience we have built at Høglund over the past 30 years,” said Peter Morsbach, Chief Executive Officer, Høglund. “As we take our next steps together as part of ABB, I am excited to build on the strengths of Høglund and ABB together, advancing marine automation for the benefit of customers worldwide.”
“By adding Høglund’s automation platform as a solution to ABB’s product portfolio, we combine advanced marine automation capabilities with global reach and an extensive service network, creating a powerful competitive advantage,” said Rune Braastad, President, ABB’s Marine & Ports division.
Image credit - ABB 
“For me, today marks a recognition of the automation technology, expertise, and experience we have built at Høglund over the past 30 years,” said Peter Morsbach, Chief Executive Officer, Høglund.

“A warm welcome to everyone at Høglund,” said Saara Kuusisto, Global Business Line Manager, Marine Systems, ABB’s Marine & Ports division. “Together, we will strengthen our automation expertise and expand our capabilities to deliver even more comprehensive integrated solutions to ships worldwide. We will build on Høglund’s distinctive values while continuing to focus on what matters most to our customers.”
Image credit - ABB 
Høglund’s integrated Automation System (IAS) is based on ABB’s control system hardware, making it a natural fit within the ABB automation portfolio. Designed for the demands of modern vessels, the modular and scalable IAS is currently installed on board more than 600 ships. It combines data from engines, generators, and cargo systems to help improve safety, energy efficiency, and operational performance.

A battery materials company has achieved a major quality certification at its first commercial-scale production plant.
Nexeon, based in Oxfordshire, UK, has announced that its facility in Gunsan, South Korea, has been awarded ISO 9001:2015 certification.
